fields.name: Veṅkaṭācārya (Vedānta Deśika)
fields.disappearance: 1371, the year he brought Śrī Raṅganātha back to Śrīraṅgam (the record's text)
fields.works: Tattva-ṭīkā (on the Śrī-bhāṣya); Śata-dūṣaṇī (cited by Jīva Gosvāmī, Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī 10.87.2); many other works for the Śrī-sampradāya
fields.notes: Vedānta Deśika of the Śrī Vaiṣṇavas (Hari-bhakti-vilāsa 15.68 ṭīkā), born 1268 near Kāñcī; refuted Advaita-vāda (Śata-dūṣaṇī). When the Muslims sacked Śrīraṅgam (1326) he had Raṅganātha taken to Tirupati, and with Goppaṇārya's help brought Him back in 1371, the year he died.

fields.name: Balarāma dāsa «Mādhavī»
fields.place: Kāmyasātpura near Rāṇāghāṭ (family); Phuliyā (boyhood); Gauḍa; Cuṭipura (his village)
fields.guru: Nityānanda Prabhu (dīkṣā); put in the care of Kānu Ṭhākura
fields.notes: Born 1478, son of Śrīdāma Taraphdār and Kṛpāmayī; learned Persian at Phuliyā, rose in Hussain Shah's army (title Khān, village Cuṭipura). Met Nityānanda on the road, who initiated him and placed him in Kānu Ṭhākura's care (#677). Wrote the Śrī Patita-pāvana-avatāra. (The disciples field said «Kanu Ṭhākura (dīkṣā)»: it was the other way round.)

Younger brother of Bhagavān Ācārya; studied Vedānta at Benares and came back a Māyāvādī. Lord Caitanya felt no joy in meeting him; Svarūpa Dāmodara refused to hear his commentary, and Bhagavān sent him home (CC Antya 2.89-100).
